summary: Commit c1a83bcab fully covers nodes that run under real Node (ryco serve and the CLI node). There, record AEAD for records of 2 KiB or more, X25519, Ed25519 verify and P-256 verify go through node:crypto behind known-answer self-tests, with noble deciding every rejection. The wiring and the parity logic check out, and no correctness bug was found. Two parts of the finding remain. (1) On desktop-hosted nodes, the packaged backend runs under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE. createCipheriv there has no chacha20-poly1305 (re-verified: Electron 44.7.0 and Bun 1.4.0 report 'Unknown cipher', and support() is chacha20Poly1305:false), so record sealing stays on noble. That was the finding's main cost: per-MiB sealing and about 9.5 ms per 3 MB screenshot frame. Electron 44.7's WebCrypto does provide ChaCha20-Poly1305 with output byte-identical to noble. I measured about 4.5x the throughput (3 MB: 9.55 ms on noble against 1.99 ms wall), and because the work runs on the libuv threadpool, the event-loop cost is only about 0.04 ms at 256 KiB and 0.3 ms at 3 MB. That route is async and experimental in Node 24, so the synchronous seam cannot use it. (2) The proposal's parity gate, which reuses the existing relay E2EE corpus with the provider installed, was not built. Section 14.7 itself says the §16 corpus MUST pass with the native implementations installed and absent, yet no corpus test installs the provider. Section 14.7 is also still marked as awaiting owner acceptance.

evidence.note: node:crypto provider: lazy known-answer gates, a 2 KiB AEAD threshold and createCipheriv('chacha20-poly1305'). The comment at lines 21-22 states that Electron's BoringSSL and Bun lack ChaCha20-Poly1305.

suiteRecordAead dispatches to native AEAD when it is installed and passed its self-test, and otherwise uses noble. The seam is synchronous. seal is called at :1217 inside async #protectCommitted, and open is called at :1416 inside synchronous #unprotect.

The packaged desktop backend (the server that runs HubConnectorLive and seals relay records for desktop-hosted nodes) runs with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, so the ChaCha known-answer test fails and records stay on noble.
The desktop main process installs the provider, but it only runs handshakes (desktopNativeE2ee*.ts) and seals no records. The comment confirms record AEAD stays on the pinned primitive.
installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives() runs when the connector service is built. HubConnectorDeferred loads it, and it runs before any NodeE2eeChannelSession seals.

makeE2eeNodeNativePrimitives().support() reports all four primitives true on Node 24.21. On Electron 44.7 run as Node and on Bun 1.4 it reports x25519, ed25519 and p256 true and chacha20Poly1305 false.

Under Electron 44.7 run as Node, subtle.encrypt ChaCha20-Poly1305 (raw-secret import) matches noble byte for byte. Wall time: 256 KiB 0.197 ms against 0.893 ms on noble, and 3 MB 1.99 ms against 9.55 ms. The synchronous issue cost on the event loop was 0.037 ms and 0.29 ms.
Section 14.7 is marked 'proposed ... recording owner acceptance ... is REQUIRED' and says 'the §16 corpus MUST pass with the native implementations installed and with them absent'.

Neither file installs the provider. git grep finds installE2eeNativePrimitives and makeE2eeNodeNativePrimitives only in relayE2eeKeys.ts, relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts and relayE2eeNodeCrypto.test.ts, and the vitest config has no setupFiles. The corpus runs only with the provider absent.

Dedicated parity tests cover X25519 low-order and non-canonical inputs, Ed25519 torsion, S+L and small-order cases, P-256 edge cases, AEAD forgeries, and one E2eeRecordSession run with and without the provider. These are solid, but they do not replace the corpus gate.

On the native Ed25519 path the public key A is decoded twice: once by isValidPublicKey in validateE2eeNodeIdentityPublicKey, and again with isSmallOrder in ed25519NativeVerdictAdmissible. R is also decoded. Measured verifyE2eeSignature: 215 us native against 710 us noble (3.3x). The raw primitive is 55 us against 680 us.
Handshake DH and keygen go through the dispatchers. The Noise CipherState AEAD (relayE2eeNoise.ts:317,332) stays on noble by design, and its messages are small.

remaining: (1) Desktop-hosted nodes: the packaged backend runs under Electron as Node (backendLauncher.ts:111), and createCipheriv lacks chacha20-poly1305 there. suiteRecordAead (relayE2eeSession.ts:404-444) therefore always falls back to noble chacha20poly1305 for sealing snapshots, screenshots and streams, which takes about 0.9 ms per 256 KiB and 9.5 ms per 3 MB frame on the event loop. A native route exists (Electron 44.7 WebCrypto ChaCha20-Poly1305), but it is async and the AEAD seam is synchronous. (2) The parity gate in the proposal and in §14.7 (docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5077) is not implemented: relayE2eeCorpus.test.ts and relayE2eeNodeCorpus.test.ts never run with the provider installed. (3) Section 14.7 still awaits owner acceptance (docs:5071-5072), although the fast paths are live in production.
fixDefects: No correctness defects found. AEAD seal is deterministic and open is tag-checked, X25519 rejects all-zero output, Ed25519 admits a native true only behind strict decode, small-order and S<L checks, P-256 admits only a native true, and every native false or throw is re-decided by noble. All four self-tests pass on Node 24.21. Gaps: the §14.7 'MUST pass the corpus with native installed' is unenforced by any test, and a minor inefficiency decodes A twice per Ed25519 native verify (relayE2eeKeys.ts:130 and :497), about 50 us of the 215 us native-path cost.
implementationSketch: A) Desktop-backend record AEAD through WebCrypto (async). In relayE2eeKeys.ts, add an optional member to E2eeNativePrimitives such as chacha20Poly1305Async { minBytes; seal(key, nonce, plaintext, aad): Promise<Uint8Array> }. In relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts, implement it with crypto.webcrypto.subtle.importKey('raw-secret', key, {name:'ChaCha20-Poly1305'}, false, ['encrypt']) and subtle.encrypt({name:'ChaCha20-Poly1305', iv: nonce, additionalData: aad}, k, plaintext). Import per record and do not cache CryptoKeys, so the key lifetime matches the createCipheriv path (§9.5). Gate it with an async RFC 8439 §2.8.2 known-answer test plus a forged-tag decrypt, started by installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives and unusable until it resolves. Enable it only when the synchronous native ChaCha is unavailable (Electron, Bun). Handle the one-time ExperimentalWarning. In relayE2eeSession.ts, give E2eeRecordAead an optional sealAsync. #protectCommitted (around 1192-1230) should await it for plaintexts at or above a tuned threshold (about 16-64 KiB) and fall back to the synchronous noble seal on rejection. Re-check #erased after the await, and treat an erase during the seal as send_failed without transmitting. Keep the plaintext-erasure finally after the await, and keep the state advance under the existing #sendQueue serialization. Leave the receive path (#unprotect, synchronous) unchanged, since records the node receives are small. Tests: sealAsync parity across sizes against noble, async known-answer failure falling back, erase during an in-flight seal, envelope parity of E2eeRecordSession with sync noble. Benchmark manually with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 apps/desktop/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron. Update §14.7 and the desktopHubStack.ts comment. B) Corpus parity gate. Wrap the top-level suites of packages/shared/src/relayE2eeCorpus.test.ts and apps/server/src/hubConnector/relayE2eeNodeCorpus.test.ts in describe.each([['pinned', undefined], ['native', makeE2eeNodeNativePrimitives()]]). Use beforeAll(() => installE2eeNativePrimitives(p)) and afterAll(() => installE2eeNativePrimitives(undefined)), and assert that support() is all true on Node in the native leg. Alternatively, export a defineCorpusSuites() and add *.native.test.ts files. C) Optional: skip the second decode of A by having validateE2eeNodeIdentityPublicKey also return the small-order verdict, or by using a small bounded per-key admissibility memo.
decisionReason: Part A changes E2EE record-sealing semantics on the send path: async AEAD, an experimental WebCrypto algorithm, and CryptoKey lifetime against §9.5 erasure. It needs a crypto and security review, and §14.7 must be updated. Section 14.7 itself is still marked as needing owner acceptance (docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5071), although the native fast paths already run in production. Part B (corpus run with the provider installed) is test-only and needs no decision.
